subject: Invoice #4531 — unexpected consumption variance and payment hold
messages:
From: Eddie Park <e.park@valorhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: accountspayable@valorhealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discrepancy on Invoice #4531 — holding payment

Hi Naomi,

Our AP team flagged Invoice #4531 (due 2025-11-29) — total looks ~3x higher than our internal consumption metrics for November. We attached our exported usage (valor-usage-Nov-2025.csv) and the PDF invoice for reference. Because this is material, we've placed the invoice on hold and want to understand the variance before releasing payment.

Key asks:
- Can you confirm the events/tokens used to calculate the invoice?
- Any known platform incidents or bulk replays that could have driven a spike around 2025-10-29 to 2025-11-02?
- We are VAT-registered in the EU; if a credit is issued, can you provide a corrected invoice reflecting reverse-charge (no VAT) — AP requires that for our records.

Please advise next steps and expected timing. We’re happy to share additional logs if useful.

Thanks,
Eddie Park
Billing Manager
Valor Health

Attachments: invoice-4531-20251101.pdf, valor-usage-Nov-2025.csv
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eddie Park <e.park@valorhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Invoice #4531 — holding payment

Hi Eddie — thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the CSV. I’m escalating this to our billing ops and your account exec so we can get a reconciliation queued immediately.

Immediate plan:
- I’ve looped in Ben (AE) and Lauren (Finance). Ben will coordinate the operational reconciliation with Rishi in billing ops.
- We’ll produce a per-minute usage export + ingestion traces for the invoice window and validate whether there were duplicate events or retries that inflated counts.
- If we confirm an overcharge, we will issue a provisional credit while we finish the audit, and follow with a corrected VAT-friendly invoice if required.

Can you confirm whether any of the timestamps in your CSV are from non-prod/test environments? Also, if you can share the earliest and latest sample timestamps you rely on (or a small sample of request IDs), that speeds the audit.

I’ll get back with a target ETA for the initial findings within 48 business hours.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Finance Partner — Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com, lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Invoice #4531 — holding payment

Hi Eddie — Ben here (account lead). Sorry for the noise — we’ll take this to root cause. A few notes from experience:
- Common causes: client-side retry loops, duplicate batch replays, or dashboard jobs that accidentally point at prod keys.
- We’ll check for significant repeated request IDs and for any elevated error-retry rates in your project during the invoice window.

Rishi — can you run a delta reconciliation between our billing events and Valor’s CSV for 2025-10-27 through 2025-11-03 and return the top 10 spike windows (by tokens) + sample request IDs? If useful, tag me and I’ll jump on a quick call with Eddie.

Eddie — if you can quickly provide (a) any IP ranges for batched jobs, (b) examples of request IDs or timestamps you consider authoritative, that will speed things up.

Thanks — will update within 48 hours.

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, Eddie Park <e.park@valorhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 14:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Invoice #4531 — holding payment (prelim findings)

Hi all — preliminary reconciliation complete (attached: prelim-recon-20251115.xlsx). Summary:

What we found:
- A concentrated spike between 2025-10-29T02:03:00Z and 2025-10-29T03:17:00Z where billed token volume shows a 3.1x increase vs your CSV for the same interval.
- Root cause appears to be a client-side retry loop: the same request IDs appear 1–6x in our ingestion logs during that 74-minute window. The pattern matches exponential backoff retries from a single IP block.
- We do not see platform-side batching or kernel anomalies during that window — the duplication originates from repeated client replays.

Numbers (rounded):
- Billed tokens in window: 92,400
- Valor reported tokens in window: ~29,900
- Delta: ~62,500 tokens (~$4,800 at your plan rate)

Proposed next steps:
1) We can issue a provisional credit of $4,800 to be applied to your next invoice while we complete a full audit (24–72 hours for final verification).
2) If you prefer a one-time refund, we can initiate a refund once the audit is complete — please advise bank or wire instructions.
3) We will produce a corrected invoice for the period with a VAT note if you confirm reverse-charge treatment.

Attachments: prelim-recon-20251115.xlsx (contains sample request IDs, the token-by-minute delta, and the IP block observed).

Eddie — can you confirm whether your batched job at 02:00–02:05Z is a retry job? If that was intended, we can discuss protecting that job via a dedicated key or routing policy to avoid future spikes.

Rishi Malhotra
Billing Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eddie Park <e.park@valorhealth.com>, accountspayable@valorhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Invoice #4531 — holding payment (resolution path)

Hi Eddie — following up with the remediation plan and next steps.

1) Provisional credit applied: We have applied a provisional credit of $4,800 to your account. This will show as a credit on your next invoice. We flagged the credit as provisional while Rishi’s team completes the full audit (expected complete by 2025-11-20 EOD PST).

2) Invoice correction & VAT: If Valor confirms reverse-charge treatment for this transaction, we will issue a corrected invoice (credit note + updated invoice) showing 0% VAT and referencing the original invoice #4531. AP: please confirm the VAT registration number and whether you want the credit applied to the next invoice or issued as a refund.

3) Preventative measures: Ben and our customer engineering team recommend issuing a dedicated service key for the batched job and enabling request-id deduplication in your integration to prevent client-side retries from inflating counts. Ben will coordinate a short technical review if you want.

4) Next update: Rishi will close the audit by 2025-11-20 and we’ll convert the provisional credit to a final credit or process a refund depending on the outcome.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — let us know the VAT registration number and preferred credit/refund routing.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Finance Partner — Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none (final corrected invoice will be provided after VAT confirmation)
